knowledge_point.title: Using the Properties of Line Integrals of Vector-Valued Functions

question.:question/problem:
![Directed segments: C_1: B to A; C_2: B to C; C_3: C to A](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179672/7ea25abfd9cc08176a78ffe7dcec795f3c3830e8fec4edf0833e57ba6b9b99ab.png)

The arrows show the orientations of the segments. The same continuous vector field $\mathbf F$ is used throughout. The closed path $C$ follows $A\to B\to C\to A$ **counterclockwise**. Which expression equals the following line integral?

$$
\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Trace the requested traversal. $C_1$ is reversed. $C_2$ is followed. $C_3$ is followed. Reversal negates a vector line integral, and additivity gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=\int_{-C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r\\&=-\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: -\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
-\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r-\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r-\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r-\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r-\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r-\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r
-\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r-\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r

generation.answer_form: -\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r+\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r

knowledge_point.title: Using the Properties of Line Integrals of Vector-Valued Functions

question.:question/problem:
![Directed segments: C_1: C to B; C_2: A to D; C_3: A to B; C_4: A to C; C_5: D to C](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179672/3d8cc3de5b7bdd3438b1db00e68f8753d458b66834f0f086b0e732266e211ac5.png)

The arrows show the orientations of the segments. The same continuous vector field $\mathbf F$ is used throughout. Let $L_1$ follow $A\to B\to C\to A$ and $L_2$ follow $A\to D\to C\to A$. You are given

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{L_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=-2\\\int_{L_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=-3\end{aligned}
$$

The closed path $C$ follows $A\to B\to C\to D\to A$ **counterclockwise**. This path is the **outer boundary**. Evaluate its line integral.

$\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=$ {{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $I_j=\int_{C_j}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r$ for each segment in its arrow direction. Trace both named loops in their given directions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{L_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=-I_1+I_3-I_4\\\int_{L_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=I_2-I_4+I_5\end{aligned}
$$

The requested outer traversal has signed sum

$$
\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=-I_1-I_2+I_3-I_5
$$

Choose the loop orientations so that their shared diagonal cancels and the outer segments have those signs:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=(-I_1+I_3-I_4)-(I_2-I_4+I_5)\\&=\int_{L_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r-\int_{L_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r\\&=(-2)-(-3)\\&=1\end{aligned}
$$

This uses orientation reversal and additivity; a closed path alone does not imply a zero integral.

question.:question/problem:
![Directed segments: C_1: A to B; C_2: C to B; C_3: A to C](/tmp/ca9837-templates-5ek4tgt5/17592186179672/67e0a4fdaac594546557c202ea94670ba63ba4e58acdd421ac0713ae6a86d71b.png)

The arrows show the orientations of the segments. The same continuous vector field $\mathbf F$ is used throughout. The closed path $C$ follows $A\to B\to C\to A$ **counterclockwise**. You are given

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=-4\\\int_{C_1}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=3\\\int_{C_2}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=4\end{aligned}
$$

Find the integral along $C_3$ in the direction of its arrows.

$\int_{C_3}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=$ {{answer}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Write $I_j=\int_{C_j}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r$ for each segment in its arrow direction. Compare each arrow with the requested traversal. Reversed segments contribute negative integrals. By additivity,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{C}\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=I_1-I_2-I_3\\-4&=(3)-(4)-I_3\\-4&=-I_3-1\\-I_3&=-3\\I_3&=3\end{aligned}
$$

The final value is in the requested arrow direction.
